$comment: Primary-source oracle — RMD cases: the Pub 590-B worked example, exact Table I/II/III divisor lookups, SECURE 2.0 trigger ages, the still-working exception, first-year April-1 deferral, and an inherited 10-year-rule year. Expected values derived independently from the cited sources; never from production code.

irs-p590b.name: IRS Publication 590-B — RMD chapter + Appendix B life expectancy tables

irs-rmd-faq.name: IRS — Retirement plan and IRA required minimum distributions FAQs
irs-rmd-faq.identifier: Withdrawals generally must start at age 73; workplace-plan participants can delay until the year they retire unless a 5% owner; reaching 73 in 2024 -> first RMD due April 1 2025 AND second due Dec 31 2025 (two RMDs in the deferral year); post-2019 deaths -> 10-year rule for non-eligible designated beneficiaries

secure2-107.name: SECURE 2.0 Act §107 (Pub. L. 117-328, Div. T) — applicable RMD age
secure2-107.accessed: 2026-07-24 (enacted §107(c) applicable-age text; the age-73 side is cross-checked against the IRS RMD FAQs and Pub 590-B 'reach age 72 after December 31, 2022 -> age 73' statements fetched the same day)
secure2-107.identifier: Applicable age 73 for those who reach 72 after 2022 (born 1951-1959); 75 for born 1960 or later (§107(c))

cases.description: The Pub 590-B worked example: age 73 in 2025, prior-year-end IRA balance $38,400, Uniform Lifetime divisor 26.5 -> IRS-published RMD $1,450.
cases.tolerance: within $1 of the IRS-published whole-dollar figure (the exact quotient is $1,449.06); divisor exact
derivation: Justin became 73 on Dec 15 2025 (born 1952 -> SECURE 2.0 trigger age 73).
RMD = 38,400 / 26.5 (Table III, age 73) = 1,449.06; Pub 590-B publishes the rounded $1,450.

cases.description: Exact Appendix B divisor lookups across all three tables, including the Table II sole-spouse >10-years-younger divisors.
derivation: Values transcribed from Pub 590-B Appendix B (accessed 2026-07-24): Table III 73/75/80; Table I (recalculating spouse mode) 55 and 62; Table II owner 75 x spouse 60 and owner 73 x spouse 63.
Non-spouse anchored mode: base age 58 -> 28.9, minus 1.0 per elapsed year (3 years -> 25.9).
§107: the applicable age is 73 for those born 1951-1959 and 75 for those born in 1960 or later.

cases.description: The §401(a)(9)(C) still-working exception: granted only on affirmative facts (current-employer plan, NOT a 5% owner, plan does not force statutory-age distributions); never available to an IRA.
derivation: IRS RMD FAQ: workplace-plan participants can delay RMDs until the year they retire, unless they are a 5% owner.
Affirmative facts on a 401(k) -> exception applies; an unknown ownership share (fivePercentOwner absent) must DENY the deferral (conservative); an IRA never qualifies.

cases.description: First-year RMD deferral to April 1 of the following year -> TWO RMDs due in that following year.
derivation: IRS RMD FAQ: reaching 73 in 2024 means the first RMD is due April 1 2025 AND the second by Dec 31 2025.
Owner at exactly the trigger age with the election -> deferred, 2 RMDs due the following year; without the election -> none from this rule.

cases.description: Inherited IRA, non-eligible designated beneficiary, owner died on/after their RBD in 2022: 10-year rule with annual distributions required in window years 1-9, full liquidation by 2032; the annual divisor is the anchored single-life schedule (longer-of vs the decedent's ghost life).
cases.tolerance: exact (rule/kind selection exact; divisor to 6 decimal places)
derivation: Owner died 2022 on/after RBD; beneficiary (OTHER_DESIGNATED, born 1965) -> 10-year rule with annual RMDs in years 1-9 (IRS RMD FAQ / Pub 590-B).
2026 is window year 4; full liquidation by 2022 + 10 = 2032.
Beneficiary schedule: base year 2023 (year after death), age then 58 -> Table I 28.9; elapsed 3 years -> divisor 25.9.
Ghost life: decedent (born 1948) was 74 at death -> Table I 15.6 - 4 = 11.6; the LONGER (larger divisor) 25.9 wins.
